You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module specifies Conway's Game of Life on a finite N×N toroidal-free grid, where N is a natural number constant (set to 4 in the model-checking configuration).

The single variable `grid` maps every position in the N×N grid (represented as pairs of integers from 1 to N) to a Boolean value, where TRUE means a cell is alive and FALSE means it is dead. The `Init` predicate allows any arbitrary initial assignment of live and dead cells across the grid. The `Next` action advances the entire grid by one generation simultaneously: a cell is alive in the next state if and only if it is currently alive with exactly 2 or 3 live neighbors, or currently dead with exactly 3 live neighbors — the standard Game of Life survival and birth rules. Cells outside the 1..N boundary are treated as permanently dead via the `sc` scoring function, which returns 0 for out-of-bounds or dead cells and 1 for live ones. The `score` function sums the contributions of the eight cardinal and diagonal neighbors to count live neighbors. The temporal specification `Spec` is `Init` conjoined with the always-enabled stuttering-tolerant next-state relation `[][Next]_vars`, with no fairness constraints. The only checked property is the type invariant `TypeOK`, asserting that `grid` remains a function from positions to Booleans.
